title: Constructed Ext restriction maps and their composition calculus
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] with Ext groups [def-pc-ext], and let $J:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be additive and preserve finite limits and finite colimits. For $A,F\in\mathcal C$, $B,E\in\mathcal D$, and isomorphisms $e:JA\cong B$, $d:JF\cong E$, define the additive homomorphism
$$q_{J,e,d,n}(x)=[d]\circ J(x)\circ[e^{-1}]:\operatorname{Ext}^n(A,F)\to\operatorname{Ext}^n(B,E).$$
If $a:F\to F$ and $b:E\to E$ obey $d\circ J(a)=b\circ d$, then $q(x\cdot[a])=q(x)\cdot[b]$. Moreover, let $G:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C_2$, $J':\mathcal C_2\to\mathcal C_4$, $G_W:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C_4$ be exact additive functors between abelian categories with Ext, and let $c:J'G\cong G_WJ$ be a natural isomorphism. Let $N\in\mathcal C_2$, $N_W\in\mathcal C_4$, $d':J'N\cong N_W$, $\varphi:GF\to N$, and $\varphi_W:G_WE\to N_W$ obey $d'\circ J'(\varphi)=\varphi_W\circ G_W(d)\circ c_F$. Define $e'=G_W(e)\circ c_A:J'GA\cong G_WB$. Then
$$q_{J',e',d',n}(G(x)\cdot[\varphi])=G_W(q_{J,e,d,n}(x))\cdot[\varphi_W].$$
These are identities of specifically constructed homomorphisms; no homomorphism is asserted bijective.

source.place: Functoriality of cohomology (01F7) and derived functors of exact functors (015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor); specialization to derived morphisms between single complexes.

proof.text: Construct q as the composition of the additive Ext map of J, precomposition with the degree-zero class of e inverse, and postcomposition with the degree-zero class of d. Each is additive by bilinearity of Ext composition. Functoriality for Ext composition and degree-zero classes and associativity give its postcomposition identity from the coefficient square.

Expand both sides of the cartesian identity using the definition of q. Rewrite J′(phi) followed by d′ using the assumed coefficient square. Separate the class of c_F by associativity and use the exact-functor-square Ext identity. The class of e′ inverse followed by c_A reduces to that of G_W(e inverse), since e′ is the specified composite isomorphism. Reassociate and use functoriality on the classes of e inverse and d to obtain the right side. These rewrites are formalized in restrictAddHom_square.

theorem restrictAddHom_square
    (G : C ⥤ D) [G.Additive] [PreservesFiniteLimits G] [PreservesFiniteColimits G]
    (J : C ⥤ C₃) [J.Additive] [PreservesFiniteLimits J] [PreservesFiniteColimits J]
    (J' : D ⥤ C₄) [J'.Additive] [PreservesFiniteLimits J'] [PreservesFiniteColimits J']
    (GW : C₃ ⥤ C₄) [GW.Additive] [PreservesFiniteLimits GW] [PreservesFiniteColimits GW]
    (c : G ⋙ J' ≅ J ⋙ GW) {A F : C} {B E : C₃} {N : D} {NW : C₄}
    (e : J.obj A ≅ B) (d : J.obj F ≅ E) (d' : J'.obj N ≅ NW)
    (φ : G.obj F ⟶ N) (φW : GW.obj E ⟶ NW)
    (h : J'.map φ ≫ d'.hom = (c.app F).hom ≫ GW.map d.hom ≫ φW)
    (n : ℕ) (x : Ext A F n) :
    restrictAddHom J' ((c.app A) ≪≫ GW.mapIso e) d' n
      ((x.mapExactFunctor G).comp (Ext.mk₀ φ) (add_zero n)) =
    ((restrictAddHom J e d n x).mapExactFunctor GW).comp (Ext.mk₀ φW) (add_zero n)
